Forwarding my quick test / troubleshooting notes. I opened the .ics Sophie attached and inspected the DTSTART/DTEND lines — they reference a local timestamp without a TZID, which can make some clients treat it as a floating time. I've pasted the relevant lines below: 

BEGIN:VEVENT
DTSTART:20260908T110000
DTEND:20260908T120000
END:VEVENT

If the organizer regenerates the invite with TZID=America/Los_Angeles (or uses the Google event editor and sets the timezone explicitly) the event will anchor correctly across clients.

Workaround: Sophie, if you can open the event > Edit > Time zone > choose "(GMT-07:00) Pacific Time - Los Angeles" and re-save, that should propagate a non-floating anchor. Alternatively we can pick a UTC time (e.g., 18:00 UTC) and everyone accept using UTC to avoid DST/floating confusion.

I'll be online for the demo either way.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
